newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major rules out VAT on food.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major rules out VAT on food.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Thursday ruled out imposing value added tax on food but said there was no need to rule out levying VAT elsewhere.

"There's absolutely no question in any terms whatsoever of VAT on food," Major told a news conference. "What we have also said is that because we have set out spending plans and taxation plans for a period there is no need to get involved in ruling out VAT."
Major said Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke had made it clear "that we don't believe it is going to be necessary."
On Wednesday, Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said Conservative central office briefings were specifically advising Conservative candidates not to rule out extending VAT.
Labour has pledged not to extend VAT to children's clothes, food, books, newspapers and public transport. Brown also reaffirmed Labour's promise to cut VAT on heating fuel to five percent from eight.
"The question for John Major and Kenneth Clarke is why will they not match Labour's commitment?" he said.
